author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects schtasks creating the task names that the MS SQL Server brute-force toolkit uses for persistence:
MicrosoftEdgeUpdateTaskMachineUA and MicrosoftEdgeUpdateTaskMachineCore with fixed GUIDs, and Microsoft_UPDATES.
The real Edge updater uses different GUIDs per install.
false_positives: Unknown
name: Scheduled Task Disguised as Microsoft Edge Update in the SQL Server Toolkit
query: process.executable.caseless:*\\schtasks.exe AND (process.command_line:(*CEC15D9B\-F4BB\-446A\-B6E1\-C61E74B016A2* OR *4C33CE3F\-7722\-4257\-AF83\-351A4911C159* OR *Microsoft_UPDATES*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a browser polling a sapper-v2 board (sapper view --serve), which fetches /__sapper_graph__/<24 hex>.json
every 2 seconds. The board has no login and shows the targets, credentials and flags of an engagement. Seen through
your proxy, someone in your network is watching a sapper-v2 engagement, often on an exposed board.
false_positives: Contest teams and testers running sapper-v2 or a fork of it
name: sapper-v2 Engagement Graph Board in Proxy Logs
query: url.original:*\/__sapper_graph__\/*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files Incalmo writes: the implant copy sandcat_tmp.go and its log /tmp/sc.log, the implant saved as splunkd outside a
Splunk bin folder, the per-command scripts dynamic_payload_<port>_<paw>.sh, the C2 state database /tmp/state_store.db, the
LLM-written exploit plugins/deception/payloads/exploit.py, the LiteLLM spend file and the per-run llm_agent.log.
false_positives: Research use of Incalmo in a lab
name: Incalmo Implant, Script or Run File Written
query: ((TargetFilename:(*\/sandcat_tmp.go OR *\/tmp\/sc.log OR *\/tmp\/state_store.db OR *\/_litellm_key_status.json OR *\/plugins\/deception\/payloads\/exploit.py)) OR (TargetFilename:*\/dynamic_payload_* AND TargetFilename:*.sh) OR (TargetFilename:*\/output\/* AND TargetFilename:*\/llm_agent.log) OR TargetFilename:*\/splunkd) AND (NOT TargetFilename:*\/bin\/splunkd*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the user agent PentestCopilot/ that Pentest Copilot (BugBase) sends when it signs in to a CTFd platform and
fetches its pages, and requests to /api/auth/registration-status, the unauthenticated API call its console makes on
the login and registration pages. In your own web logs the second means you serve a Pentest Copilot console.
false_positives: CTF players using Pentest Copilot on a CTFd platform you run
Another application with the same API path
name: Pentest Copilot User Agent or Console API in Web Logs
query: user_agent.original:PentestCopilot\/* OR url.path:\/api\/auth\/registration\-status

author: ThreatDefence
description: A web server, runtime or database process started a shell, download tool or netcat. ARTEX agents explore a host this way after exploiting a web application.
name: Web or Database Service Spawns a Shell or Download Tool
query:
process where event.type == "start" and
  process.parent.name in ("nginx", "httpd", "apache2", "php-fpm", "java", "node", "mysqld", "mariadbd", "postgres",
                          "w3wp.exe", "httpd.exe", "java.exe", "node.exe", "php-cgi.exe", "sqlservr.exe", "mysqld.exe") and
  process.name in ("sh", "bash", "dash", "curl", "wget", "nc", "ncat", "socat", "busybox",
                   "cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "curl.exe", "certutil.exe", "bitsadmin.exe")

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a lookup of a name whose first label starts with neurosploit, the prefix of every out-of-band token
NeuroSploit puts in blind SSRF, XXE, command injection and JNDI payloads (<token>.<operator domain>). A lookup proves
a resolver saw the payload; NeuroSploit itself treats it as weaker than an HTTP callback. neurosploitai.github.io is
the project's documentation site.
false_positives: Authorized tests with NeuroSploit
name: NeuroSploit Out-of-Band Callback Name Lookup
query: dns.question.name:/[nN][eE][uU][rR][oO][sS][pP][lL][oO][iI][tT].*/ AND (NOT dns.question.name:/[nN][eE][uU][rR][oO][sS][pP][lL][oO][iI][tT][aA][iI]\..*/)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects AutoPT, an LLM penetration testing agent from a research benchmark: its CLI (python main.py --name
<service/CVE> --ip_addr <IP>), the upstream engine's CLI (autopt run --benchmark-name ... --ip-addr ...), and the
full-port SYN scan its scan prompt tells the model to run (nmap -sS -p- --min-rate 3000 -T4). The nmap command line
is an example in the prompt, so the model may vary it.
false_positives: Researchers running the AutoPT benchmark against its own vulhub targets
Other scripts that take --name and --ip_addr arguments, or an administrator who types the same nmap command
name: AutoPT Agent Started or Running Its Scan Steps
query: (process.command_line:*main.py* AND process.command_line:*\-\-name\ * AND process.command_line:*\-\-ip_addr\ *) OR (process.command_line:*autopt* AND process.command_line:*\-\-benchmark\-name* AND process.command_line:*\-\-ip\-addr*) OR process.command_line:*nmap\ \-sS\ \-p\-\ \-\-min\-rate\ 3000\ \-T4\ *

author: ThreatDefence
description: Five or more deployments validate calls from one caller in one minute, the capability check ARTEX agents run with a stolen Azure identity.
false_positives: Automation and infrastructure-as-code pipelines. Baseline before alerting
name: Azure Resource Manager Validate Sweep

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the files CAI (Cybersecurity AI, aliasrobotics/cai) writes under ~/.cai: the per-session log
cai_<uuid>_<time>_<user>_<os>_<ip>.jsonl in ~/.cai/logs (uploaded to logs.aliasrobotics.com by its telemetry),
the API backend's user database api_auth.json and its key, and the continuous-ops run folders.
false_positives: Security teams and researchers running CAI
name: CAI Session Log, API Auth Database or Workspace Written
query: TargetFilename:/.*[\/\\]\.cai[\/\\]logs[\/\\]([A-Za-z0-9_-]+_)?cai_[0-9a-f-]{36}_[0-9]{8}_[0-9]{6}_.*\.jsonl/ OR (TargetFilename:(*\/.cai\/api_auth.json OR *\/.cai\/api_auth.json.key OR *\\.cai\\api_auth.json OR *\\.cai\\api_auth.json.key)) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/.cai\/continuous_ops\/run_* OR *\\.cai\\continuous_ops\\run_*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a file named .emulation_marker_<TTP_ID>, which Cyber-AutoAgent's threat_emulation module tells the model
to create for every technique it runs on a host. The name comes from the prompt, so the model may vary it.
false_positives: Authorized adversary emulation with Cyber-AutoAgent
name: Cyber-AutoAgent Threat Emulation Marker File
query: TargetFilename:(*\/.emulation_marker_* OR *\\.emulation_marker_*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the processes H-Pentest starts for an assessment: dirsearch from the path its backend image installs it to
(/app/tools/dirsearch/dirsearch.py) with --random-agent and JSON output, nuclei with the template folder of that image
(/app/tools/nuclei-templates) and a rate limit of 150, and the Python scripts it runs inside its sandbox container,
written to /sandbox/workspace_<epoch>/script_<milliseconds>.py. H-Pentest is a contest-oriented LLM penetration testing
platform (FastAPI backend, Vue console, Docker sandbox).
false_positives: Authorized use of H-Pentest
Other images that install dirsearch or nuclei templates under /app/tools
name: H-Pentest Scanner Command Line or Sandbox Script
query: (process.command_line:*\/app\/tools\/dirsearch\/dirsearch.py* AND process.command_line:*\-\-random\-agent* AND process.command_line:*\-\-format\=json*) OR (process.command_line:*nuclei* AND process.command_line:*\/app\/tools\/nuclei\-templates* AND process.command_line:*\-rate\-limit\ 150*) OR (process.command_line:*python3\ \/sandbox\/workspace_* AND process.command_line:*\/script_*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a process whose command line carries a PentestGPT system prompt. PentestGPT starts the Claude Code CLI
through claude-agent-sdk, which passes the prompt as an argument: --append-system-prompt with the Supervisor or
Executor instructions on current main, --system-prompt with the CTF solver prompt in v1.0.0. Both run with
--permission-mode bypassPermissions. Codex receives the instructions over its app-server protocol, so this rule
does not see the Codex backend.
false_positives: Authorized tests, CTF practice and research runs with PentestGPT
name: Claude Code Started With a PentestGPT System Prompt
query: process.command_line:(*You\ are\ the\ Supervisor\ for\ an\ authorized\ penetration\ test.* OR *You\ are\ the\ Executor\ for\ an\ authorized\ penetration\ test.* OR *You\ are\ PentestGPT,\ an\ AI\-powered\ CTF\ challenge\ solver*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects CAI (Cybersecurity AI) uploading its session log to https://logs.aliasrobotics.com/upload (and
/upload/intermediate), its licence check GET https://api.aliasrobotics.com:666/key/info, and pip reaching Alias's
private package index on packages.aliasrobotics.com:664 with the API key in the URL path.
false_positives: Authorized use of CAI or other Alias Robotics products
name: CAI Telemetry Upload or Alias Gateway in Proxy Logs
query: url.domain:/[lL][oO][gG][sS]\.[aA][lL][iI][aA][sS][rR][oO][bB][oO][tT][iI][cC][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR (url.domain:/[aA][pP][iI]\.[aA][lL][iI][aA][sS][rR][oO][bB][oO][tT][iI][cC][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ AND url.original:*\/key\/info*) OR url.domain:/[pP][aA][cC][kK][aA][gG][eE][sS]\.[aA][lL][iI][aA][sS][rR][oO][bB][oO][tT][iI][cC][sS]\.[cC][oO][mM]/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects RedAmon's self-naming user agents (RedAmon-AISurfaceRecon/1.0, RedAmon-CachePoison/1.0 and the
"compatible; RedAmon" strings), the XSS canary rEdAm0n1337XsS its agent is told to use in every parameter, and the
rdmncb cache buster of its cache poisoning tests. All are defaults of the published code.
false_positives: Authorized tests with RedAmon
name: RedAmon User Agent or Canary in Web Logs
query: user_agent.original:*RedAmon* OR (url.query:(*rEdAm0n1337XsS* OR *rdmncb\=cb*)) OR cs-referer:*rEdAm0n1337XsS*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the user agent PentestCopilot/ that Pentest Copilot (BugBase) sends to CTFd platforms, and requests to the
console API path /api/auth/registration-status, which a user's browser calls when it opens a Pentest Copilot
login or registration page.
false_positives: CTF players using Pentest Copilot
Another application with the same API path
name: Pentest Copilot User Agent or Console API in Proxy Logs
query: user_agent.original:PentestCopilot\/* OR url.original:*\/api\/auth\/registration\-status*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects lookups of the Decepticon telemetry gateway (decepticon-telemetry-gateway.purpleailab.workers.dev), which
the launcher's setup wizard enables unless the operator declines, and of decepticon.red, which serves the installer
and the hosted console.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Decepticon
Visits to the Decepticon web site (selection_site)
name: Decepticon Telemetry or Installer Domain Lookup
query: (dns.question.name:/[dD][eE][cC][eE][pP][tT][iI][cC][oO][nN]-[tT][eE][lL][eE][mM][eE][tT][rR][yY]-[gG][aA][tT][eE][wW][aA][yY]\.[pP][uU][rR][pP][lL][eE][aA][iI][lL][aA][bB]\.[wW][oO][rR][kK][eE][rR][sS]\.[dD][eE][vV]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[dD][eE][cC][eE][pP][tT][iI][cC][oO][nN]-[tT][eE][lL][eE][mM][eE][tT][rR][yY]-[gG][aA][tT][eE][wW][aA][yY]\.[pP][uU][rR][pP][lL][eE][aA][iI][lL][aA][bB]\.[wW][oO][rR][kK][eE][rR][sS]\.[dD][eE][vV]/) OR (dns.question.name:/[dD][eE][cC][eE][pP][tT][iI][cC][oO][nN]\.[rR][eE][dD]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[dD][eE][cC][eE][pP][tT][iI][cC][oO][nN]\.[rR][eE][dD]/)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the X-ARTX-KEY request header and ARTEX probe marker strings in requests. Community-
reported, so treat a match as a lead and confirm with other activity from the same source.
false_positives: Authorized penetration tests that use ARTEX
name: ARTEX Probe Marker in HTTP Request
query: (url.query:(*ARTEX_WRITE_PROBE* OR *ARTX_PERSIST_OK* OR *artex_control_marker_zz9q* OR *ARTEX\-PROBE\-* OR *artex\-probe\-*)) OR cs-headers:*X\-ARTX\-KEY*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects requests to the WSUS administration, reporting or server-sync web services. JPCERT/CC Case E reports attacks
on internet-facing WSUS servers by operators using Cairn, CyberStrikeAI and ARTEX. These services should not answer
the internet; client endpoints are excluded.
false_positives: Internal WSUS administration consoles and downstream servers reaching the log source
name: WSUS Administration or Sync API Requested
query: url.path:(*\/ApiRemoting30\/WebService.asmx* OR *\/ServerSyncWebService\/ServerSyncWebService.asmx* OR *\/ReportingWebService\/ReportingWebService.asmx*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects use of an AutoPT web console's API (configuration with model keys, system info, agent runs), its upstream
user agent AutoPT/1.0, and the request AutoPT makes before each Inquire step: a vulhub README from
raw.githubusercontent.com with a Chrome user agent cut off before "(KHTML, like Gecko)". The console has no login,
so a request to these paths from outside the operator's host is someone else using it.
false_positives: Researchers running the AutoPT benchmark
Other Flask apps with the same API paths (selection_console alone is weak; check the response for the AutoPT page title)
name: AutoPT Console API or Vulhub PoC Fetch in Proxy Logs
query: (url.original:(*\/api\/task\/start* OR *\/api\/system\/info* OR *\/api\/docker\/envs*)) OR user_agent.original:AutoPT\/* OR (url.original:*\/vulhub\/vulhub\/master\/* AND user_agent.original:"Mozilla\/5.0 \(Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64\) AppleWebKit\/537.36")

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the commands Incalmo uses to put its implant (MITRE Caldera's Sandcat) on a new host: the copy named sandcat_tmp.go,
the reachability check "curl ... -w C2:%{http_code}", the curl download with the header file:sandcat.go, an implant started
with "-server http... -group red", and the implant saved as splunkd as the model prompts suggest.
false_positives: MITRE Caldera exercises, which start Sandcat with the same -server and -group red arguments
Research use of Incalmo in a lab
name: Incalmo Spreading a Caldera Sandcat Implant
query: (process.command_line:(*sandcat_tmp.go* OR *C2\:%\{http_code\}* OR *file\:sandcat.go*)) OR (process.command_line:*\ \-server\ http* AND process.command_line:*\ \-group\ red*) OR (process.executable:*\/splunkd AND process.command_line:*\ \-server\ http*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the DarkMoon autonomous penetration testing stack on a host: its launcher starting a campaign
(opencode run --agent pentest with a TARGET line, through docker compose exec), its Docker Hub images
ascit/darkmoon and ascit/opencode-darkmoon, and the wrappers that start its MCP server and live log console
(darkmoon-mcp, darkmoon-cli, and docker exec -i darkmoon darkmoon-mcp for the stdio transport).
false_positives: Authorized tests with DarkMoon
name: DarkMoon AI Pentest Agent Launcher, Containers or MCP Server
query: (process.command_line:*opencode* AND process.command_line:*\-\-agent\ pentest* AND process.command_line:*TARGET\:*) OR process.command_line:/(.*([\/ ]))?darkmoon\.sh(([ ]).*)?/ OR (process.command_line:(*ascit\/darkmoon* OR *ascit\/opencode\-darkmoon*)) OR (process.command_line:(*darkmoon\-mcp* OR *darkmoon\-cli*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects how CHYing-agent runs model-written Python in its Kali tools container: a Docker exec of
/bin/bash -c "echo <base64> | base64 -d | python3" whose base64 starts with the work-directory header the agent
prepends to every script (# === 自动注入：工作目录设置 ===). The header is fixed in the code, so its base64 prefix
is the same on every call made with a challenge work directory.
false_positives: Authorized tests or contest work with CHYing-agent
name: CHYing-agent Python Tool Call in Its Kali Container
query: process.command_line:*IyA9PT0g6Ieq5Yqo5rOo5YWl77ya* AND process.command_line:*base64\ \-d* AND process.command_line:*python3*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects Vigilo running (certeu/vigilo at 82c2d353): its white-box worker (src.temporal.worker on a vigilo- task
queue), its grey-box worker (src.greybox_web.worker), its API (src.webapi.main), the helper commands its agents run
(vigilo-record, save-deliverable), and the coding agent CLIs it starts with approvals off whose prompt contains
"authorised security assessment run by Vigilo".
false_positives: Security teams running Vigilo
name: Vigilo Platform or White-Box Agent on a Host
query: (process.command_line:(*src.temporal.worker\ \-\-serve\ \-\-task\-queue\ vigilo\-* OR *\-m\ src.greybox_web.worker* OR *\-m\ src.webapi.main* OR *\/usr\/local\/bin\/vigilo\-record* OR *vigilo\-record\ show\ * OR *vigilo\-record\ verdict\ * OR *vigilo\-record\ lead\ *)) OR (process.command_line:*authorised\ security\ assessment\ run\ by\ Vigilo* AND (process.command_line:(*\-\-dangerously\-skip\-permissions* OR *\-\-dangerously\-bypass\-approvals\-and\-sandbox*)))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects touch /tmp/success in a request query, the default command_to_execute that the research PentestAgent
(nbshenxm/pentest-agent) gives its execution agent as proof of code execution. Vulhub uses the same command in its
examples, so a match is an attempt to prove code execution, by this agent or by someone following Vulhub.
false_positives: Authorized tests and labs that use the Vulhub proof command
name: PentestAgent (Paper Code) Default Proof Command in Web Logs
query: url.query:(*touch\ \/tmp\/success* OR *touch%20\/tmp\/success* OR *touch\+\/tmp\/success* OR *touch%20%2Ftmp%2Fsuccess* OR *touch\+%2Ftmp%2Fsuccess* OR *touch$\{IFS\}\/tmp\/success*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files attackers write into Hermes Agent's home folder: the godmode jailbreak prefill file and skill folder, the
loot folder Carbonato's GH0ST persona fills with stolen keys, and Carbonato's persistence files.
false_positives: Researchers installing Hermes optional security skills
name: Hermes Agent Jailbreak, Loot or Carbonato Files Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/.hermes\/loot\/* OR *\/.hermes\/skills\/security\/godmode\/*)) OR TargetFilename:*\/.hermes\/prefill.json OR (TargetFilename:\/opt\/gh0st\/* OR (TargetFilename:(\/usr\/local\/bin\/.docker\-network\-monitor OR \/usr\/sbin\/systemd\-logind)))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a browser or script using a remote H-Pentest backend through a proxy (the unauthenticated configuration dump
/api/v1/config/all, task intervention and continue endpoints, the task WebSocket path /api/v1/ws/ws/), and the
downloads its backend Dockerfile makes through the gh-proxy.org GitHub mirror when the image is built (nuclei-templates,
sqlmap, dirsearch).
false_positives: Other applications with an /api/v1/config/all endpoint
Other projects that clone these repositories through gh-proxy.org
Authorized use of H-Pentest
name: H-Pentest Console API or Image Build Download Through a Proxy
query: (url.original:(*\/api\/v1\/config\/all* OR *\/api\/v1\/ws\/ws\/*)) OR (url.original:*\/api\/v1\/tasks\/* AND (url.original:(*\/intervention OR *\/continue))) OR (url.original:(*gh\-proxy.org\/https\:\/\/github.com\/projectdiscovery\/nuclei\-templates* OR *gh\-proxy.org\/https\:\/\/github.com\/sqlmapproject\/sqlmap* OR *gh\-proxy.org\/https\:\/\/github.com\/maurosoria\/dirsearch*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects DNS lookups of strix.gateway.scarf.sh, which Strix calls at the start and end of every scan and for every
finding unless STRIX_TELEMETRY is turned off.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Strix
name: Strix Telemetry DNS Query
query: dns.question.name:/[sS][tT][rR][iI][xX]\.[gG][aA][tT][eE][wW][aA][yY]\.[sS][cC][aA][rR][fF]\.[sS][hH]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[sS][tT][rR][iI][xX]\.[gG][aA][tT][eE][wW][aA][yY]\.[sS][cC][aA][rR][fF]\.[sS][hH]/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects Pentest Swarm AI writing its consent file and log under the user's home folder. authorization.log gets one
JSON line for every real target (time, target, scope, method, user), so it is also the first file to read on a host
where the tool was found.
false_positives: Penetration testers running Pentest Swarm AI
name: Pentest Swarm AI Authorization Record Written
query: TargetFilename:(*\/.pentestswarm\/authorization.* OR *\\.pentestswarm\\authorization.*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects Xalgorix running: the binary or its container image, and the shell wrapper it puts in front of every
command the agent runs (export XALGORIX_WORKSPACE=..., the __xalgorix_resolve_path function, and xalgorix-scan-init
when it runs as root). Xalgorix is an autonomous penetration testing agent that needs no approval for tool calls.
false_positives: Bug bounty hunters and security teams running Xalgorix
name: Xalgorix Agent on a Host
query: process.executable:*\/xalgorix OR (process.command_line:(*XALGORIX_WORKSPACE\=* OR *__xalgorix_resolve_path* OR *xalgorix\-scan\-init* OR *xalgord\/xalgorix* OR *xalgorix\ \-\-web*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects outbound or reverse-proxy requests whose user agent names the ARTEX framework or its renamed
builds. Outbound hits mean a host on your network is running ARTEX.
false_positives: Authorized penetration tests that use ARTEX
name: ARTEX Agentic Attack Framework User Agent in Proxy Logs
query: user_agent.original:(*artex\-readonly\/* OR *artex\-pentest\/* OR *artex\-audit\/* OR *artex\-verify\/* OR *artex\-spawn\/* OR *ARTEX\-worker\/* OR *artex\-enrich\/* OR *artex\-i21861\-canary* OR *artex\-agent* OR *artex\-judge\-* OR *ARTeX\-authorized\-pentest* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ ARTeX* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ \(ARTEX\)* OR *ArtExVerify\/* OR *ArtEx\/1.0* OR *scopeweaver* OR *spa\-api\-recon*)

author: ThreatDefence
description: Detects the HexStrike tool server, its MCP client, and tools started by the server.
false_positives: Authorized red team use of HexStrike
name: HexStrike Server or MCP Client Process
query: (process.command_line:(*hexstrike_server.py* OR *hexstrike_mcp.py*)) OR process.parent.command_line:*hexstrike_server.py*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a certificate or secret added to an application or service principal. Storm-0940 used
compromised applications to add credentials to other applications and assign themselves roles.
Review who or what made the change: an application changing another application is the case to
chase.
false_positives: Administrators rotating application secrets
name: Credential Added to an Entra ID Application
query: azure.auditlogs.operation_name:("Update application \- Certificates and secrets management" OR "Add service principal credentials")

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the CyberStrikeAI implant's Linux cron persistence, (crontab -l; echo '@reboot <implant> &') | sort -u | crontab -,
and its curl_beacon one-liner, a bash loop that POSTs to /check_in with an X-Implant-Token header every 5 seconds.
false_positives: Administrators adding @reboot jobs the same way (cron selection only)
name: CyberStrikeAI Implant Linux Persistence or curl Beacon
query: (process.command_line:*@reboot* AND process.command_line:*sort\ \-u\ \|\ crontab\ \-*) OR process.command_line:*X\-Implant\-Token*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the LaunchAgent the CyberStrikeAI implant writes on macOS, ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.apple.systemupdate.plist,
with RunAtLoad and KeepAlive. Apple does not ship a per-user agent with this label.
false_positives: Unknown
name: CyberStrikeAI Implant LaunchAgent com.apple.systemupdate
query: TargetFilename:*\/Library\/LaunchAgents\/com.apple.systemupdate.plist

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the files Cyber-AutoAgent writes on the host that runs it: the operation log and report in
outputs/<target>/OP_<timestamp>/, the optimized execution prompt, and the front end's settings file
~/.cyber-autoagent/config.json, which can hold model provider keys.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Cyber-AutoAgent
name: Cyber-AutoAgent Operation Files Written
query: ((TargetFilename:(*\/OP_* OR *\\OP_*)) AND (TargetFilename:(*cyber_operations.log OR *security_assessment_report.md OR *execution_prompt_optimized.txt))) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/.cyber\-autoagent\/config.json* OR *\\.cyber\-autoagent\\config.json*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the user agents of AutoPT's ReadHTML tool: AutoPT/1.0 in the upstream engine, and in evenhu9/AutoPT a
Chrome string cut off before "(KHTML, like Gecko)", which no browser sends. The truncated string is also used by
CyberStrikeAI's implant and appears in a Xalgorix prompt example, so it names a family of tools, not AutoPT alone.
false_positives: Authorized tests with AutoPT
Other tools that send the same truncated Chrome string
name: AutoPT Page Reader User Agent in Web Logs
query: user_agent.original:(AutoPT\/* OR "Mozilla\/5.0 \(Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64\) AppleWebKit\/537.36")

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the PentestGPT command-line tools starting a run: pentestgpt-agent and pentestgpt-agent-audit (current
main), the module form python -m pentestgpt_agent.trial, pentestgpt with --target and its other options (v1.0.0),
pentestgpt-benchmark (v1.0.0) and pentestgpt-legacy (the interactive version from the paper).
false_positives: Authorized tests, CTF practice and research runs with PentestGPT
name: PentestGPT AI Pentest Agent Command Line
query: process.command_line:/(.*([\/\\ "']))?pentestgpt-agent(-audit)?(\.exe)?["']?[ ](.*[ ])?--(goal|target|run-dir|expected-flag|resume|backend)[ =].*/ OR (process.command_line:(*\-m\ pentestgpt_agent.trial* OR *\-m\ pentestgpt_agent.audit*)) OR process.command_line:/(.*([\/\\ "']))?pentestgpt(\.exe)?["']?[ ](.*[ ])?(--target|-t|--non-interactive|--no-telemetry|--list-sessions|--session-id)[ =].*/ OR process.command_line:/(.*([\/\\ "']))?pentestgpt-(benchmark|legacy|legacy-connection)(\.exe)?((["']|[ ]).*)?/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects requests to the BOAZ routes of a Hexstrike-redteam server in the logs of a web server or reverse proxy in
front of it. The server has no authentication, so a request from an unexpected address means someone else can
build payloads and run commands on it.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Hexstrike-redteam
name: Hexstrike-redteam BOAZ API in Web Server Logs
query: url.path:(\/api\/boaz\/generate\-payload* OR \/api\/boaz\/list\-loaders* OR \/api\/boaz\/list\-encoders* OR \/api\/boaz\/analyze\-binary* OR \/api\/boaz\/validate\-options*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files Cairn writes on a worker host: graph.yaml task snapshots under /tmp/cairn-prompts/, the Pi worker's
models.json with the provider API key under /tmp/cairn-pi/, and the tsec-actions skill from the Tencent TCH
competition setup that operators' worker images still carry.
false_positives: Authorized red team use of Cairn
name: Cairn Task Snapshot, Pi Provider Key or Competition Skill Written
query: TargetFilename:(*\/tmp\/cairn\-prompts\/* OR *\/tmp\/cairn\-pi\/* OR *\/skills\/tsec\-actions\/SKILL.md*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects Cyber-AutoAgent fetching or seeding its prompts in Langfuse (/api/public/v2/prompts/cyber/system/...,
/cyber/report/...), and browsing of the Langfuse project its compose file seeds (cyber-project-id).
false_positives: Another Langfuse project that names its prompts cyber/system/ or cyber/report/
name: Cyber-AutoAgent Langfuse Prompt Fetch or Project Page in Proxy Logs
query: (url.original:(*\/api\/public\/v2\/prompts\/cyber\/system\/* OR *\/api\/public\/v2\/prompts\/cyber\/report\/*)) OR url.original:*\/project\/cyber\-project\-id*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a lookup of the hosts pentest-ai uses: telemetry.pentestai.xyz (opt-in telemetry), app.pentestai.xyz
(cloud dashboard sync with a ptai_ key) and r.pentestai.xyz, the open redirect canary host its oracle puts in
redirect parameters. A lookup of r.pentestai.xyz from one of your servers means something followed that redirect.
false_positives: Security teams running pentest-ai with telemetry or cloud sync on
name: pentest-ai Telemetry, Cloud Sync or Redirect Canary Lookup
query: dns.question.name:/[tT][eE][lL][eE][mM][eE][tT][rR][yY]\.[pP][eE][nN][tT][eE][sS][tT][aA][iI]\.[xX][yY][zZ]/ OR dns.question.name:/[aA][pP][pP]\.[pP][eE][nN][tT][eE][sS][tT][aA][iI]\.[xX][yY][zZ]/ OR dns.question.name:/[rR]\.[pP][eE][nN][tT][eE][sS][tT][aA][iI]\.[xX][yY][zZ]/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects NeuroSploit testing a web server: its user agent NeuroSploit/<version>, the soft-404 probe path
/nrsplt_baseline_404_check_9x7 it requests at the start of every run, the NEUROSPLOIT canaries it puts in paths and
parameters (NEUROSPLOITsub<hex> soft-404 checks, NEUROSPLOITnsxss<hex> XSS payloads), its open redirect test host
neurosploit.example, and the user agent of its web shell manager. All strings are in the NeuroSploit code at 54d8e860.
false_positives: Authorized tests with NeuroSploit
name: NeuroSploit Scan Markers in Web Logs
query: (user_agent.original:(NeuroSploit\/* OR *NeuroSploit\-WebShell\/*)) OR (url.path:(*nrsplt_baseline_404_check_9x7* OR *NEUROSPLOITsub*)) OR (url.query:(*NEUROSPLOITns* OR *neurosploit.example* OR *oob.invalid*))

author: ThreatDefence
description: Placeholder probe paths, alg none JWTs or the fixed OAuth callback probe that ARTEX sends while mapping a web application.
name: ARTEX Web Probe Artifacts
query: url.original : (*zzz-nonexistent-xyz123* or *zzz_nonexistent_abc.txt* or *Notexist-xyz* or *eyJhbGciOiJub25lI* or *eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJub25lI* or *eyJhbGciOiJOb25lI* or *eyJhbGciOiJOT05FI* or *code=AAAA&state=notvalidb64!!*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the LazyOwn red team framework on a host: the C2 server (python3 -W ignore lazyc2.py <port> <user> <password>,
which puts the operator password on the command line), the MCP server an AI agent drives (skills/lazyown_mcp.py,
skills/lazyown_mcp_opencode.py, or with --sse on 127.0.0.1:9871), the CLI (lazyown.py) and the all-in-one launcher
fast_run_as_r00t.sh with its tmux session lazyown_sessions and sessions/c2_launch.sh. Also the documented install
(curl of raw.githubusercontent.com/grisuno/LazyOwn/main/bootstrap.sh) and the container ghcr.io/grisuno/lazyown.
false_positives: Authorized tests with LazyOwn
Developers working on the LazyOwn code
name: LazyOwn C2 Server, MCP Server or Launcher Started
query: (process.command_line:(*lazyc2.py* OR *lazyown_mcp.py* OR *lazyown_mcp_opencode.py* OR *fast_run_as_r00t.sh* OR *sessions\/c2_launch.sh*)) OR (process.command_line:*python3* AND process.command_line:*lazyown.py*) OR (process.command_line:*tmux* AND process.command_line:*lazyown_sessions*) OR (process.command_line:(*raw.githubusercontent.com\/grisuno\/LazyOwn\/* OR *ghcr.io\/grisuno\/lazyown*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the Agent Zero image being run, its UI starting inside the container, and its tunnel server that publishes the
UI to the internet. Agent Zero ships a hacker profile on a Kali base; GTIG reported threat-actor experimentation with it.
false_positives: Developers and researchers running Agent Zero
name: Agent Zero Container, UI or Tunnel Started
query: process.command_line:(*agent0ai\/agent\-zero* OR *self_update_manager.py\ docker\-run\-ui* OR *\/a0\/run_tunnel.py*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the page readers of AI agent CLIs: Qwen Code, Kimi CLI, opencode and Claude Code (which Cairn's workers
run with DeepSeek behind it). Agents read target pages with these while curl, Python and Kali tools do the rest.
Ordinary users send the same strings, so treat a hit as context and correlate with scanning from the same address.
false_positives: Developers and users of these agents reading public pages
name: AI Agent Page Reader User Agent in Web Server Logs
query: user_agent.original:*Claude\-User\ \(claude\-code\/* OR (user_agent.original:(QwenCode\/* OR KimiCLI\/* OR opencode\/*))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects command lines that only Cairn produces: the Codex worker's model_provider="cairn" override, the Pi worker's
--provider cairn and /tmp/cairn-pi/ agent folder, the dispatcher and server entry points, and the cairn-dispatch-
worker containers.
false_positives: Authorized red team use of Cairn
name: Cairn Agent Worker or Dispatcher Command Line
query: process.command_line:(*model_provider\=\"cairn\"* OR *model_providers.cairn.base_url* OR *\-\-provider\ cairn* OR *\/tmp\/cairn\-pi\/* OR *\/tmp\/cairn\-prompts\/* OR *cairn\ dispatch\ \-\-config* OR *cairn\-dispatch\-* OR *cairn\-worker\-container*)

author: ThreatDefence
description: Detects requests to PentAGI's update endpoint or to console API paths that only PentAGI uses.
false_positives: Approved PentAGI deployments
name: PentAGI Console API Requested Through a Proxy
query: url.original:*\/api\/v1\/proxy\/updates\/pentagi\/check* OR url.domain:/[uU][pP][dD][aA][tT][eE]\.[pP][eE][nN][tT][aA][gG][iI]\.[cC][oO][mM]/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a download of the kali-linux-headless metapackage, which HackSynth installs in every new attackbox
(docker_setup.py:36). The kalilinux/kali-rolling image fetches packages over plain HTTP from http.kali.org, so the
package name is in the proxy log. Anyone installing the same metapackage in a Kali system or container matches too.
false_positives: Kali installs and container builds that use the kali-linux-headless metapackage
name: Kali Headless Metapackage Download, as in HackSynth Attackbox Setup
query: url.original:*kali\-linux\-headless*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the result file AutoPT writes after each agent run:
src/result/<model folder>/<service>_<CVE>_<model>_FSM.jsonl, with the commands the agent ran and whether the
exploit worked.
false_positives: Researchers running the AutoPT benchmark
name: AutoPT Run Result Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/result\/* OR *\\result\\*)) AND TargetFilename:*_FSM.jsonl

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects lookups of dalfox-xss-test.com, the blind XSS callback Cyber-AutoAgent's general module gives dalfox. A
lookup from a browser or server you own means a stored payload ran there.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Cyber-AutoAgent
name: Cyber-AutoAgent Dalfox Blind XSS Callback DNS Query
query: dns.question.name:/[dD][aA][lL][fF][oO][xX]-[xX][sS][sS]-[tT][eE][sS][tT]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/.*\.[dD][aA][lL][fF][oO][xX]-[xX][sS][sS]-[tT][eE][sS][tT]\.[cC][oO][mM]/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the NyxStrike tool server (nyxstrike_server.py), its MCP client (nyxstrike_mcp.py), its launcher
(nyxstrike.sh) and its virtual environment (nyxstrike-env), and every tool the server starts: the server runs each
tool through /bin/sh -c with itself as the parent. NyxStrike is a HexStrike derivative that exposes about 200
offensive tools to an AI assistant or its own LLM agents.
false_positives: Authorized red team or lab use of NyxStrike
name: NyxStrike Server, MCP Client or Tool Started by the Server
query: (process.command_line:(*nyxstrike_server.py* OR *nyxstrike_mcp.py* OR *nyxstrike.sh* OR *\/nyxstrike\-env\/bin\/python*)) OR process.parent.command_line:*nyxstrike_server.py*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the research PentestAgent (nbshenxm/pentest-agent, arXiv 2411.05185) running: its recon, planning and
execution scripts, and the exact cvemap and searchsploit command lines its planning agent builds. The recon and
execution agents run every command the model returns through /bin/sh -c, so look at the children of the matched
python process. Not the GH05TCREW/pentestagent tool, which has its own folder.
false_positives: Researchers reproducing the PentestAgent paper or running it in a lab
Other projects with scripts named agents/recon_agent.py
name: PentestAgent (Paper Code) Agents, cvemap or searchsploit Run on a Host
query: (process.command_line:(*agents\/recon_agent.py* OR *agents\/planning_agent.py* OR *agents\/execution_agent.py*)) OR (process.command_line:*cvemap\ * AND process.command_line:*\ \-l\ 50\ * AND process.command_line:*\ \-offset\ * AND process.command_line:*\ \-j*) OR (process.command_line:*\|\ cvemap\ \-json\ \>\ * AND process.command_line:*\/info\/cvemap.json*) OR (process.command_line:*searchsploit\ * AND process.command_line:*\ \-j\ \>\ resources\/* AND process.command_line:*\/exploitdb.json*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects FilterLogEvents calls whose filter pattern searches for passwords or AWS access keys.
Datadog saw a stolen key search CloudWatch logs with patterns such as ?password ?AKIA, always with a
limit of 1000.
false_positives: Engineers searching logs for leaked secrets during a cleanup
name: CloudWatch Logs Searched for Secrets
query: (event.provider:logs.amazonaws.com AND event.action:FilterLogEvents) AND (aws.cloudtrail.request_parameters:(*password* OR *AKIA* OR *secret* OR *token*))

author: ThreatDefence
description: A process or file carries the names ARTEX agents give their own test artifacts.
name: ARTEX Artifact Names on a Host
query:
any where
  (event.category == "process" and process.command_line : ("*artex-probe-*", "*ArtexProbe*", "*artx5v*", "*art18-*", "*ARTEX_WRITE_PROBE*", "*ARTX_PERSIST_OK*")) or
  (event.category == "file" and (file.name : "artex-probe-*" or file.path : "*ProgramData*artx5v*" or
     file.name in ("cl1217.jsp", "f1219a.jsp", "z1219.jsp", "zzartx0000.php")))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects strings DarkMoon's agent prompts put in requests: the user agent dm-edge (the edge-proxy agent's first
request, curl -sSI -A dm-edge), the cache buster dmcb=DM1 of its cache poisoning test, and a container registry
manifest tagged darkmoon-proof-<random> when it proves it can push images. The model usually copies these
commands from the prompt but may change them.
false_positives: Authorized tests with DarkMoon
name: DarkMoon Probe Markers in Web Server Logs
query: user_agent.original:dm\-edge OR url.query:*dmcb\=DM1* OR url.path:*\/manifests\/darkmoon\-proof\-*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the Shannon CLI started with --exp-php2shell. The probe sends a control request and up to two multipart
bodies of about 1 MiB and 7.4 MiB, flooded with MIME headers, to one URL. It is designed to crash a PHP worker on an
unpatched runtime (CVE-2026-109618 as the Shannon source names it) and runs from the CLI, without Docker.
false_positives: Administrators checking their own PHP servers after the php2shell fixes
name: Shannon Experimental php2shell Crash Probe Started
query: process.command_line:*\-\-exp\-php2shell* AND process.command_line:*shannon*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects lookups of update.pentagi.com and support.pentagi.com. Every PentAGI installation checks for updates every
three hours by default, so a hit shows where PentAGI runs.
false_positives: Approved PentAGI deployments
name: DNS Query for the PentAGI Update Service
query: dns.question.name:/[uU][pP][dD][aA][tT][eE]\.[pP][eE][nN][tT][aA][gG][iI]\.[cC][oO][mM]/ OR dns.question.name:/[sS][uU][pP][pP][oO][rR][tT]\.[pP][eE][nN][tT][aA][gG][iI]\.[cC][oO][mM]/

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects an MCP client driving a remote Hexstrike-redteam server's BOAZ routes: /api/boaz/generate-payload,
/api/boaz/list-loaders, /api/boaz/list-encoders, /api/boaz/analyze-binary or /api/boaz/validate-options.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Hexstrike-redteam
name: Hexstrike-redteam BOAZ API Requested Through a Proxy
query: url.original:(*\/api\/boaz\/generate\-payload* OR *\/api\/boaz\/list\-loaders* OR *\/api\/boaz\/list\-encoders* OR *\/api\/boaz\/analyze\-binary* OR *\/api\/boaz\/validate\-options*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files PentestAgent by GH05TCREW writes: its token counter loot/token_usage.json, the named pipes of a child
agent (/tmp/pa_mcp_<random>/mcp_in.fifo and mcp_out.fifo), the PID file of its detached MCP manager
(~/.pentestagent/mcp.pid) and its TUI reports (loot/reports/report_<timestamp>.md). loot/notes.json is written too
but is a common name, so it only counts here next to token_usage.json in a hunt.
false_positives: Bug bounty hunters, red teams and security teams running PentestAgent
name: PentestAgent (GH05TCREW) Loot, Child Agent Pipes or Daemon PID File Written
query: TargetFilename:*\/loot\/token_usage.json OR (TargetFilename:*\/pa_mcp_* AND (TargetFilename:(*\/mcp_in.fifo OR *\/mcp_out.fifo))) OR TargetFilename:*\/.pentestagent\/mcp.pid OR (TargetFilename:*\/loot\/reports\/report_* AND TargetFilename:*.md)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files CHYing-agent writes on the operator's host or in its tools container: the per-target work folder
agent-work/ctf/<Category>/<challenge>/ with findings.log, attack_timeline.md, progress.md, dumps/commands.log and
poc_scripts/poc_<time>.py, its SQLite database data/chying.db, its run logs logs/chying_agent_<time>.log, and the
data folder ~/.taie/null-zone/ of its Null Zone contest skills.
false_positives: Security teams and contest players running CHYing-agent
name: CHYing-agent Work Folder, Database or Log Files Written
query: (TargetFilename:*\/agent\-work\/ctf\/* AND (TargetFilename:(*\/findings.log OR *\/attack_timeline.md OR *\/dumps\/commands.log OR *\/dumps\/execution_summary.md OR *\/dumps\/reflection_history.md))) OR ((TargetFilename:*\/agent\-work\/ctf\/* AND TargetFilename:*\/poc_scripts\/poc_*) AND TargetFilename:*.py) OR TargetFilename:*\/data\/chying.db OR (TargetFilename:*\/logs\/chying_agent_* AND TargetFilename:*.log) OR TargetFilename:*\/.taie\/null\-zone\/*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the Incalmo C2 server (incalmo/c2server/c2server.py), its Celery worker and beat (incalmo.c2server.celery.celery_worker),
and the Metasploit RPC daemon its attacker container starts with the fixed password "password". The C2 server listens on
0.0.0.0:8888 with no authentication and hands shell commands to Caldera Sandcat implants on compromised hosts.
false_positives: Research or red team use of Incalmo in a lab
Other setups that start msfrpcd with the password "password"
name: Incalmo C2 Server or Its Celery Worker
query: (process.command_line:(*incalmo\/c2server\/c2server.py* OR *incalmo.c2server.celery.celery_worker*)) OR (process.command_line:*msfrpcd* AND process.command_line:*\-P\ password*)

author: ThreatDefence
description: Failed sign-ins for 20 or more distinct accounts from one address in 30 minutes. Storm-0940 sprayed 327 accounts at a fixed one-second rhythm. The native KQL and SPL hunts also test the rhythm.
false_positives: Automation and infrastructure-as-code pipelines. Baseline before alerting
name: Password Spray Against Many Entra ID Accounts From One Address

author: ThreatDefence
description: Detects HexStrike's hard-coded user agents and the <hexstrikeXSSTest123> reflection probe its browser agent submits.
false_positives: Authorized tests with HexStrike
name: HexStrike User Agent or XSS Probe in Web Logs
query: (user_agent.original:(*HexStrike\-HTTP\-Framework\/* OR *HexStrike\-BrowserAgent\/* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ \(Compatible\ Exploit\)*)) OR url.query:*hexstrikeXSSTest123*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects Carbonato's escape from a privileged container into the host (nsenter -t 1 -m -u -n -i), its worm container
names and image, and its persistence paths. Carbonato installs Hermes Agent with a GH0ST persona on each host.
false_positives: Node maintenance scripts that enter the host namespaces and download or schedule something
name: Carbonato Docker Worm Host Escape or Persistence
query: ((process.command_line:*nsenter* AND process.command_line:*\-t\ 1* AND process.command_line:*\-m\ \-u\ \-n\ \-i*) AND (process.command_line:(*curl\ * OR *wget\ * OR *crontab* OR *chattr* OR *authorized_keys* OR *systemctl\ enable* OR *rc.local* OR *.hermes*))) OR (process.command_line:(*netns\-probe* OR *system\/resolved* OR *.docker\-network\-monitor* OR *\/opt\/gh0st\/* OR *CARBONATO_API_KEY*)) OR process.executable:\/usr\/sbin\/systemd\-logind

author: ThreatDefence
description: Detects Okta events whose raw user agent names ARTEX.
false_positives: Authorized penetration tests that use ARTEX
name: ARTEX User Agent in Okta System Log
query: client.userAgent.rawUserAgent:(*artex\-readonly\/* OR *artex\-pentest\/* OR *artex\-audit\/* OR *artex\-verify\/* OR *artex\-spawn\/* OR *ARTEX\-worker\/* OR *artex\-enrich\/* OR *artex\-i21861\-canary* OR *artex\-agent* OR *artex\-judge\-* OR *ARTeX\-authorized\-pentest* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ ARTeX* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ \(ARTEX\)* OR *ArtExVerify\/* OR *ArtEx\/1.0* OR *scopeweaver* OR *spa\-api\-recon*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects an app role or directory role assigned to a service principal. ARTEX agents in the
Storm-0940 campaign had compromised applications grant themselves roles. Investigate when the
initiator is the same service principal that receives the role.
false_positives: Administrators granting application permissions
name: App Role or Directory Role Assigned to a Service Principal
query: azure.auditlogs.operation_name:("Add app role assignment to service principal" OR "Add member to role")

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects sqlservr.exe starting cmd.exe or PowerShell, the result of xp_cmdshell. The SQL Server toolkit seen in
ARTEX operations enables xp_cmdshell after brute-forcing the sa login, then downloads its loader.
false_positives: Database jobs that use xp_cmdshell by design. Baseline per server
name: SQL Server Spawns a Shell Through xp_cmdshell
query: process.parent.executable.caseless:*\\sqlservr.exe AND (process.executable.caseless:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files the Virga C2 framework writes on the operator host: the server's extension store under
/tmp/virga/extensions, its SQLite database data/virga.db, the CLI history .virga_history, the CLI JSONL log
logs/virga-<datetime>.jsonl, the generator's temporary folder virga-generator-<random>, and the local model the
beacons carry, internal/implant/llama/models/model.gguf.
false_positives: Red teams and researchers running Virga
Another application that names its database virga.db
name: Virga Server, Generator or Model Files Written
query: TargetFilename:\/tmp\/virga\/extensions\/* OR (TargetFilename:(*\/data\/virga.db OR *\/.virga_history OR *\/internal\/implant\/llama\/models\/model.gguf OR *\\internal\\implant\\llama\\models\\model.gguf)) OR (TargetFilename:(*\/virga\-generator\-* OR *\\virga\-generator\-*)) OR (TargetFilename:*\/logs\/virga\-* AND TargetFilename:*.jsonl)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects an image pushed to a container registry under a repository named after an attack agent or a write test:
artex-i<issue id>, hermes-h<id>-writecheck, csai-push-probe, xalgorix-pwn, the gh0st/ and fsociety/ namespaces, or
names that hold writecheck, push-probe or pwned. Agents that find a registry open to pushes prove it by pushing a
small image, and they name it after themselves. Open registries on the internet carry these names by the hundred.
A push can be followed by a poisoned copy of one of your own images, so check what else that source pushed.
false_positives: Security teams testing their own registry
A project of your own with one of these words in its name
name: Attack Agent Write Test on a Container Registry
query: (cs-method:PUT AND url.path:\/v2\/* AND url.path:*\/manifests\/*) AND ((url.path:(*writecheck* OR *write\-check* OR *push\-probe* OR *push\-poc* OR *push\-test* OR *pwned* OR *hijack\-canary* OR *regscan\-probe* OR *probe\-write\-test* OR *\/gh0st\/* OR *\/gh0st\-* OR *\/fsociety\/* OR *\/csai\-* OR *\/cyberstrike\-probe* OR *\/xalgorix\-*)) OR url.path:/.*\/(artex[-_](i[0-9]|probe|push|poc|rce|test|exploit|retest)|ptx-i[0-9]|hermes-h[0-9]).*/)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a Run value named SystemUpdate, which the CyberStrikeAI implant writes under
HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run to start at logon.
false_positives: Software that really names its Run value SystemUpdate
name: CyberStrikeAI Implant Run Key Value SystemUpdate
query: registry.path:*\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\SystemUpdate

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a Run value named NSUpdate, which NeuroSploit's C2 writes under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run
to start its PowerShell beacon at logon.
false_positives: Software that really names its Run value NSUpdate
name: NeuroSploit Beacon Run Key Value NSUpdate
query: registry.path:*\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\NSUpdate

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a value written under HKLM\SOFTWARE\EmulationMarkers\, where Cyber-AutoAgent's threat_emulation module
tells the model to record each technique it runs. The key comes from the prompt, so the model may vary it.
false_positives: Authorized adversary emulation with Cyber-AutoAgent
name: Cyber-AutoAgent Threat Emulation Marker Registry Key
query: registry.path:*\\SOFTWARE\\EmulationMarkers\\*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the user agent PentestAgent by GH05TCREW sets on its headless Chromium: the Chrome string cut off after
AppleWebKit/537.36, which no real browser sends. The CyberStrikeAI implant and an Xalgorix curl example use the same
string, so match the whole value and look at what else the address sent before attributing it.
false_positives: CyberStrikeAI implants and other tools that send the same truncated string
Authorized tests with PentestAgent
name: PentestAgent (GH05TCREW) Browser Tool User Agent in Web Logs
query: user_agent.original:("Mozilla\/5.0 \(Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64\) AppleWebKit\/537.36" OR Mozilla\/5.0\+\(Windows\+NT\+10.0;\+Win64;\+x64\)\+AppleWebKit\/537.36)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the Virga command and control framework running on a host: its server (virga-server, which opens an
unauthenticated admin API and MCP servers on 8443, 8444 and 50012), its operator CLI (virga-cli), its MCP stdio
server (virga-mcp-stdio), the make targets that start them, and the MCP Inspector scripts that point at them.
Virga's beacon can carry a local language model that runs commands on the compromised host by itself.

author: ThreatDefence

author: ThreatDefence

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the command CyberStrikeAI's webshell manager runs on every new webshell, "echo :OSPROBE_%OS%:END", which
shows up as a shell started by the web server process.
false_positives: Authorized tests with CyberStrikeAI

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the files Vigilo (certeu/vigilo at 82c2d353) writes in a repository it assesses: the run folder
.vigilo/<session>/ with its agents/, prompts/ and deliverables/ folders, the .vigilo-remote-url file, and the Git

author: ThreatDefence
description:

no legitimate use against a production SSO route.
false_positives: Security scanners testing for JWT signature bypass

query: url.query:(*eyJhbGciOiJub25lI* OR *eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJub25lI* OR *eyJhbGciOiJOb25lI* OR *eyJhbGciOiJOT05FI* OR *eyJhbGciOiJub25lIiwidHlwIjoiSldUIn0.* OR *eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJub25lIn0.*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects a web server, application runtime or database process starting a shell, download tool or
network utility. ARTEX agents run discovery and pull tooling this way after exploiting a web
application, in quick succession and in short bursts.
false_positives: Application servers that run shell scripts by design. Baseline each service before alerting
name: Web or Database Service Spawns a Shell or Download Tool on Linux
query: (((process.parent.executable:(*\/nginx OR *\/httpd OR *\/apache2 OR *\/php\-fpm OR *\/mysqld OR *\/mariadbd OR *\/postgres)) OR process.parent.executable:*\/php\-fpm*) OR ((process.parent.executable:(*\/java OR *\/node)) AND (user.name:(www\-data OR apache OR nginx OR http OR tomcat OR tomcat9 OR jetty OR jboss OR wildfly OR node OR nodejs OR nobody OR daemon)))) AND (process.executable:(*\/sh OR *\/bash OR *\/dash OR *\/curl OR *\/wget OR *\/nc OR *\/ncat OR *\/socat OR *\/busybox))

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects Decepticon traffic in the logs of a web server it tests or exposes: a user agent with the Decepticon/
token, a user agent template from its opsec skill sent with the placeholder unfilled (<CHROME_VER>, <FIREFOX_VER>,

traffic comes from ordinary tools and impersonated browsers, so absence of a match means little.

name: Decepticon Markers in Web Server Logs
query: (user_agent.original:(*Decepticon\/* OR *\<CHROME_VER\>* OR *\<FIREFOX_VER\>* OR *\<CURRENT_VER\>*)) OR url.path:\/_decepticon\/*

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the CAI (Cybersecurity AI, aliasrobotics/cai) command line started as an API backend, Textual UI, with

Alias's private index on packages.aliasrobotics.com:664); its continuous-ops loop runner; and the Kali container
its /virtualization command starts as kali-security with host networking and seccomp off.

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects PentestAgent by GH05TCREW running: the pentestagent console script or python -m pentestagent with its
subcommands, the MCP server mode (which listens on 0.0.0.0:8080 without authentication by default), the child

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects files Shannon writes on the host that runs it: the run state in <workspace>/.shannon/ (session.json,

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects processes that only Decepticon's containers start: the sandbox command daemon (python3 -m
decepticon_sandbox.server on port 9999), its web and browser runners (python3 -I -m decepticon_sandbox.web or

name: Decepticon Sandbox, Agent Server or C2 Container Process
query: (process.command_line:(*decepticon_sandbox.server* OR *decepticon_sandbox.web* OR *decepticon_sandbox.browser* OR *@dcptn_completion*)) OR (process.command_line:(*decepticon.cli\ time\-window\-resume* OR *\/app\/litellm_startup.py*)) OR (process.command_line:*sliver\-server\ operator* AND process.command_line:*\-\-name\ decepticon*) OR (process.command_line:*teamserver\ server* AND process.command_line:*\/opt\/havoc\/profiles\/havoc.yaotl*)

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects the user agents Decepticon's own HTTP clients send from the host that runs it: decepticon-telemetry/1.0 to
its telemetry gateway, decepticon-roe/1 to crt.sh when an engagement is created, decepticon-http-sandbox/1 to its

name: AWS Access Denied Sweep Across Many APIs

author: ThreatDefence
description:
Detects an attack tool whose parent is an AI agent CLI or the shell Claude Code runs commands through
(zsh -c source ~/.claude/shell-snapshots/... on Linux and macOS, the CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL_LAUNCHER_SCRIPT PowerShell
launcher on Windows). Auto-approve flags are not part of the rule: staff use them too, and an agent can run an
attack tool without one. Qwen Code, Kimi CLI, Codex and opencode start tools through a plain shell, which puts the
agent one level above the parent, so this rule only sees them when they start the tool directly; the KQL hunt in
behaviors/sentinel/hunting covers the grandparent. The model behind the agent does not matter.
Tools written in Python, Ruby or Perl (sqlmap, NetExec, Metasploit, nikto and others) run under their interpreter,
so the image is python3, ruby or perl and the tool is the script in the command line; the script selections cover
them. A tool started as a module (python3 -m) is not covered.
Agents installed with npm or pip run under node or python and are found by their package path in the parent
command line.
